- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at 10-15% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0) and price is trending upward, model lags; forecast 1-2 days ahead of true price.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in 30d horizon, apply downward bias of 1-3% per 10-day window.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “+1.0” spikes, model tends to overreact; dampen forecast by 5-10% for next 5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10-15 day windows; if forecast is >10% above 10-day moving average, reduce by 2-5%.
- If true outcome is below 65.00 and sentiment is neutral, model often overcorrects; forecast should be capped at 65.00–68.00.
